meta.name: Authentication and Account Recovery
meta.description: Focused authentication, verification, activation, and account-recovery layout with limited distraction and explicit security feedback.

purpose: Enable users to establish or recover an authenticated session with minimal distraction, strong field clarity, safe error handling, and no exposure of implementation-specific security details.
useWhen: The route performs login, multifactor verification, account activation, password recovery, session recovery, or identity confirmation.
The user must complete a focused security-sensitive task.
The application shell is intentionally unavailable or suppressed.
doNotUseWhen: The screen is a marketing landing page.
The user is editing profile settings while authenticated.
The route presents general product documentation.
Security architecture details are being shown as product benefits.

selectionQuestions: Which identifiers or credentials are requested?
What feedback may be disclosed without revealing account existence?
How are rate limits, lockouts, and expired links represented?
Is MFA required, optional, or conditional?
What is the recovery path after session expiration?
Which branding content is useful without distracting from authentication?

regions.name: Brand Context
regions.role: Provide restrained product identity and approved trust context without competing with the authentication task.
regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible, with reduced content on compact layouts.

compact.notes: Hide nonessential illustration before reducing form clarity.

medium.placement: Above or beside the authentication panel.
medium.layout: Compact brand identity with optional concise supporting text.
medium.notes: Do not create large empty decorative space.

wide.placement: Left side of a split layout or above a centered panel.
wide.layout: Brand identity with restrained illustration or trust context.
wide.notes: The authentication panel remains the primary focus.

ultrawide.placement: Left side of a constrained split layout.
ultrawide.layout: Brand identity with restrained approved visual.

rules: Brand identity remains consistent with the application.
Security implementation details are not user-facing promotional content.
Environment indication appears only when users may access non-production environments.
Images must not lower text contrast or distract from the form.

regions.name: Authentication Panel
regions.role: Contain route orientation, fields, errors, primary submission, and approved recovery links.
prohibitedComponents: Duplicate login button outside the panel

scroll.notes: The complete authentication page uses one ordinary vertical scroll owner.

compact.layout: Single-column full-width panel with safe horizontal margins.
compact.notes: Controls use full available panel width.

medium.placement: Centered below or beside brand context.

wide.placement: Right side of split layout or centered.
wide.notes: The panel does not stretch with the viewport.

ultrawide.placement: Right side of constrained split layout.

rules: One visible heading identifies the active authentication task.
Fields have visible labels.
The primary action is unambiguous.
Recovery links remain discoverable but visually secondary.
Errors do not disclose whether an account exists unless approved.

regions.name: Security Feedback
regions.role: Communicate invalid credentials, expired links, lockout, rate limit, verification, and session states safely.

compact.placement: Inside the authentication panel before affected fields.

wide.notes: Do not use global toast as the only feedback.

rules: Messages are safe against account enumeration.
Rate-limit and lockout feedback follows the approved disclosure policy.
Expired session and expired link states provide a clear recovery action.
Technical details remain in logs.

regions.name: Alternative Authentication
regions.role: Provide approved identity-provider, passkey, recovery-code, or alternative authentication methods.
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible only when alternative methods are configured and eligible.

compact.placement: Inside the authentication panel after the primary method.

wide.notes: One approved provider button per configured method.

rules: Alternative methods are clearly labeled.
The active recommended method remains identifiable.
External provider navigation explains context when necessary.

regions.name: Legal and Support
regions.role: Provide required policy, privacy, accessibility, and support access without distracting from authentication.
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when legally or operationally required.

wide.placement: Bottom of the constrained authentication layout.
wide.notes: Do not create a full application footer.

ultrawide.placement: Bottom of the constrained authentication layout.

rules: Required legal links remain available.
Support paths do not reveal account existence.
Links have clear destinations and focus behavior.

composition.columnPolicy: Single authentication column on compact and medium layouts; optional constrained brand and authentication split on wide layouts.
spacingOwnership: The layout owns spacing between brand context, authentication panel, and legal links.
AuthenticationPanel owns spacing between heading, fields, feedback, alternatives, and primary action.
FormField owns label, control, help, and error spacing.
surfacePolicy: The authentication panel uses one clear surface.
Brand context may render directly on the canvas.
Do not mix unrelated light and dark component themes.
Feedback uses semantic warning or danger treatment.
rules: Authentication remains the dominant task.
The panel remains constrained.
Brand content remains secondary.
Security implementation details remain hidden.
prohibited: Redundant login action in both global header and form.
JWT, RLS, hashing, token, API, or cryptography details shown as user-facing content.
Background image that reduces form contrast.

actions.primaryPlacement: Inside the authentication panel after the active credentials or verification controls.
actions.secondaryPlacement: Recovery links, alternative authentication methods, or return navigation.
actions.overflowPolicy: Rare alternative methods may move to an accessible alternative-method menu.
actions.compactBehavior: Primary authentication action becomes full width; alternative methods stack.
rules: One primary authentication action is dominant.
Recovery remains secondary but discoverable.
Pending state prevents duplicate authentication attempts.
Button labels describe the current authentication stage.

content.headingPolicy: One h1 identifies the authentication task; supporting explanations use ordinary body text.
content.longContentPolicy: Error, recovery, and legal text support localization expansion without widening the panel.
content.truncationPolicy: Do not truncate authentication instructions, errors, or recovery actions.
content.emptyStatePlacement: Not normally applicable; missing or expired authentication context becomes a dedicated recovery state.
content.loadingStrategy: Use a concise authentication bootstrap or pending state without exposing protected application content.
content.errorScope: Credential, verification, rate-limit, and recovery errors remain inside the authentication panel; application bootstrap errors use a dedicated safe state.
rules: Messages use clear user language.
Credential errors avoid unnecessary disclosure.
Security state is explained without implementation jargon.
The product name and identity remain consistent.

responsive.zoomExpectation: Authentication must remain usable at 200% zoom where practical and at minimum 125% browser zoom.
responsive.internalOverflowPolicy: The document may scroll vertically; the authentication panel must not create nested ordinary scrolling.

transformations.change: Keep the split layout constrained and avoid enlarging decorative brand content.
transformations.reason: Authentication clarity does not improve through excessive visual scale.

transformations.change: Move brand context above the authentication panel or reduce it to a compact identity block.
transformations.reason: The form requires a predictable centered width.

transformations.change: Use a single-column layout, compact brand identity, full-width controls, and stacked alternative methods.
transformations.reason: Compact viewports require direct task focus and usable touch targets.

states.rendering: Resolve authentication bootstrap or verification context without briefly rendering protected application content.
Render the active authentication, verification, activation, or recovery stage.
Communicate expiring session, remaining recovery limitation, or non-blocking security attention.
states.userAction: Continue or take the recommended recovery action.

states.rendering: Render safe authentication feedback without exposing technical provider responses or account existence.
Render the relevant sign-in or session-recovery stage.
Render a safe authentication-service unavailable state.
Show pending sign-in, code verification, recovery request, or activation state and prevent duplicate submission.
Explain that a link, code, or session context expired and present the approved restart action.
states.userAction: Request a new link, code, or session.

landmarkMap: The authentication panel uses the primary main landmark.
Brand identity uses a header region when appropriate.
Legal and support links use a footer landmark.
Authentication feedback uses alert or status semantics.
headingStructure: One h1 identifies the active authentication stage.
Supporting content does not introduce unnecessary heading levels.
keyboard: All fields, code inputs, links, and provider actions are keyboard operable.
Submission works through expected keyboard interaction.
Focus returns appropriately after recoverable errors.
Password visibility controls have accessible names.
announcements: Authentication errors are associated with the panel or field.
Pending state and successful stage transition are perceivable.
Expired session or link state is announced.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Error, pending, verification, expired, and disabled states do not depend only on color.
rules: Credential fields have visible labels.
One-time-code inputs expose an understandable accessible model.
Autofill and password-manager behavior must not be unnecessarily blocked.
Focus indicators remain visible on every interactive element.

prohibitedPatterns: Technical authentication architecture shown to users.
Low-contrast decorative background behind the form.
Credentials stored or logged by presentation components.
dataMagnitude: Names, email addresses, recovery messages, and legal links may expand through localization.
Verification codes may vary in length according to the approved authentication provider.
performance: Authentication routes should load minimal required code.
Do not load the complete authenticated application before session success.
Avoid unnecessary third-party scripts on security-sensitive routes.
implementation: Follow the approved backend authentication architecture.
Do not expose authentication tokens to visual components.
Use the canonical form and error layers.
Preserve safe return-navigation behavior after authentication.
Machine presence conditions come from presenceDefaults; visibilityCondition prose is explanatory only.

presenceDefaults.rationale: Authentication routes retain restrained product identity even when compact layouts reduce decorative brand content.
The active authentication or recovery task always requires the primary authentication panel.
Security feedback occupies space only when a security-relevant message or recovery state exists.
Alternative methods appear only when configured and eligible for the active authentication stage.
Legal and support links appear only when required by policy or the active recovery flow.

checks.description: The authentication recipe must validate against the layout recipe schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing recipe fields.

checks.description: Credential fields, recovery links, errors, and primary submission must be keyboard accessible and properly labeled.
checks.remediation: Correct form semantics, labels, and focus behavior.

checks.description: Authentication feedback must not disclose unsafe account, provider, token, or implementation details.
checks.remediation: Normalize messages through the approved security error policy.

checks.description: The authentication panel must remain usable without horizontal overflow across approved compact and wide viewports.
checks.remediation: Correct panel width, split transformation, or content wrapping.

checks.description: Pending authentication must prevent duplicate submission and protected content must not render before session resolution.
Authentication optional regions must render only from typed security-feedback, alternative-method, and legal/support presence signals.
checks.remediation: Correct craftDefaults/presenceDefaults and keep conditional regions required=false with cardinality.minimum=0.

examples.name: Email and password login
examples.description: Product identity, labeled credential fields, safe errors, primary login action, password recovery, and legal links.

examples.name: Multifactor verification
examples.description: Verification orientation, code input, resend behavior, expiration feedback, recovery method, and safe pending state.
